newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea's KSFC supplies funds for more margin loans.
newsitem.headline: Korea's KSFC supplies funds for more margin loans.

text.p: The Korea Securities Financing Corp said on Wednesday it had supplied 200 billion won to brokerage houses to offer additional margin loans to investors.
A spokesman for the company said the fund supply, aimed at supporting the sagging stock market, took effect immediately.
"We have decided to supply the fund as the local stock market has been languishing due mainly to short liquidity," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
The fund will be supplied at an annual interest rate of 10 percent, compared with the nation's bank lending rates averaging at over 12 percent, he said.
The corporation was set up jointly by the nation's major financial companies but the government is widely seen as retaining a strong influence on the corporation's operations.
On Tuesday, the finance ministry denied media reports that the ministry was planning steps to boost the stock market.
A huge overhang of margin loans amid declining fund inflow into the market has been a major factor behind the recent sluggishness of the bourse, brokers said.
The outstanding loans for margin trading were estimated at 2.9 trillion won as of Monday, compared with 2.5 trillion won worth of customer deposits at brokerage houses, they said.
They added that between 500 billion and 900 billion won in such loans had to be repaid this month.
